do_not_assume: The Rock name is the App Store name.
The API key secures a Lava webhook.
A saved template is valid after Lava renders.
A preview proves production-shell behavior.
goal: A Rock-managed application with a valid Start Screen and documented baseline settings.
steps: Confirm Rock 14 or later.
Open `Admin Tools > CMS Configuration > Apple TV Apps`.
Create the application record with an internal name and description.
Review Application Styles, Enable Page Views, API Key, Page View Retention Period, and Authentication Page.
Save the record.
Open the generated Start Screen.
Add a minimal supported TVML template.
Render any Lava and validate the final TVML.
Select cacheability from the page’s sensitivity and freshness requirements.
Test through the exact target or demo shell.
title: Recipe: Create a minimal Rock Apple TV application

do_not_assume: HTML elements or browser CSS work.
Template behavior is portable.
Public caching is appropriate for personalized content.
goal: A new page that emits valid TVML and uses an intentional cache policy.
steps: Select the TVML template that most closely matches the journey.
Create the page from the intended application.
Give it a clear internal name and description.
Write TVML using only supported elements for the selected template.
Add Lava using documented page merge fields.
Render the Lava output with anonymous and signed-in states where relevant.
Validate the rendered output as TVML.
Choose Public, Private, No-Cache, or No-Store.
Add navigation to the page through a documented Rock command.
Test focus, Back navigation, Light and Dark themes, and cached reload behavior.
title: Recipe: Add a cache-aware TVML page

do_not_assume: Lava double braces work for the auth fields.
A visible QR image proves authentication completion.
A code remains valid beyond the configured lifetime.
Source behavior from `develop` matches the installed release.
goal: A viewer can authenticate from a phone or computer by scanning a QR code or entering a short code.
steps: Create an external Rock web page.
Add the Remote Authentication block.
Associate the block with the intended TV application site.
Establish the external URL or route.
Set that page as the application’s Authentication Page.
Create the TV login page.
Display `{ authQrCodeUrl }`, `{ authCode }`, and the external page URL.
Create a timeout page with a clear route home.
Select a success page.
Add the `login` command with the login, timeout, and success page GUIDs.
Retain navigation-stack clearing unless the tested journey requires otherwise.
Test QR, manual-code, timeout, failure, success, and Back-button paths.
title: Recipe: Implement remote sign-in

do_not_assume: YouTube is supported.
A watch map alone appends to the old interaction.
Successful playback proves tracking succeeded.
goal: A supported media file plays with intentional resume and interaction behavior.
steps: Select `playVideo` for MP4 or HLS, or `playAudio` for MP3.
Supply the direct media URL.
Add title, subtitle, artwork, and description when required.
Associate the Rock Media Element and related entity when watch tracking requires them.
Decide the interaction outcome before adding resume parameters.
Add `rockWatchMap` when a prior resume position is required.
Add `rockInteractionGuid` only when progress must append to that existing interaction.
Test initial playback.
Stop partway through and retest resume.
Verify whether the expected interaction was appended or newly created.
Confirm the command is `playVideo` or `playAudio`.
Confirm video uses a direct MP4 or HLS source.
Confirm audio uses a direct MP3 source.
Reject YouTube as a supported source for these commands.
Inspect the exact media URL and metadata parameters.
If Rock watch tracking is expected, inspect the Media Element and related-entity parameters.
Test the same media without interaction parameters to separate playback failure from tracking failure.
title: Recipe: Add tracked video or audio playback

do_not_assume: Browser CSS support.
A native-app reference layout is reproducible in TVML.
A single theme test is sufficient.
Keep shadow offsets and blur close enough to avoid wrapper clipping.
goal: Text, badges, images, and focus states remain legible in both Light and Dark themes.
steps: Start with predefined `tv-text-style` values.
Add font weight or family only where the design requires it.
Add Light and Dark media-query branches.
Inspect badge tint and image contrast in each theme.
Add text shadows only when necessary.
Keep shadow offsets and blur close enough to avoid wrapper clipping.
Test system-selected themes.
Test any page-level theme override.
Test focus and highlighted states with the remote.
title: Recipe: Build a theme-safe styling pass

do_not_assume: Flattened icons retain parallax.
LSR works in place of LCR.
Historical Top Shelf dimensions are current App Store requirements.
goal: A delivery set contains the documented icon, launch, Top Shelf, and optional parallax assets.
steps: Create three-layer app icons.
Export PNG foreground layers and a JPG background layer.
Export icon sets at 400 × 240, 800 × 480, and 1280 × 768.
Export static launch images at 1920 × 1080 and 3840 × 2160.
If Top Shelf assets are required, export the documented standard or wide PNG sizes.
If content parallax is required, produce an LCR file.
Host the LCR at a direct URL.
Verify that no LSR file was substituted.
Test focus, parallax, and launch appearance in the target shell.
Reconfirm current Apple packaging requirements before final submission.
title: Recipe: Prepare the application image package

do_not_assume: Demo success proves App Store packaging.
Demo support exists in every compiled shell.
Clearing settings is reversible without knowing the compiled destination.
goal: The community shell loads the intended Rock application configuration for bounded testing.
steps: Verify that the demo-request form and Rock Core application remain available.
Request a demo key.
Install or open Rock Core on Apple TV.
Open the Demo screen.
Enter the key.
Restart the application.
Confirm the loaded application identity.
Test page rendering, navigation, themes, authentication, and media separately.
Use `clearDemo` when the intended outcome is to restore compiled settings.
title: Recipe: Test through demo mode

do_not_assume: Lava webhooks are secured by default.
An application API key automatically protects the webhook.
One installation’s handler behavior proves another installation’s state.
goal: The agent can state what a Lava webhook exposes and whether its protection has been verified.
steps: Resolve the exact request URL and HTTP verb.
Identify the matching Lava Webhook Defined Value.
Read the complete Lava template.
Inventory its request inputs and output fields.
Inventory every enabled Lava command.
Identify any person or sensitive data that can be returned.
Verify the actual security layer outside the webhook.
Test unauthorized behavior with a bounded, read-only request.
Record only a public-safe conclusion.
Stop before launch if the endpoint relies on default webhook security.
title: Recipe: Review a Lava API before connecting it to Apple TV
